beats.say: Think of it like this. A metre of plain cotton cloth from one mill looks exactly like a metre from the next. So the buyer picks the cheapest. And whenever there's too much capacity, which in textiles was most of the time, prices fall to the bare cost of running the machines. Nothing is left to pay back the money that bought them.
